cinema.intro: Buy tickets and popcorn for a film, then find a good book in the library next door. Learn film and book words and how to say what you think about a story.
cinema.item.3d-glasses.s1: Do we need 3D glasses for this film?
cinema.item.3d-glasses.s2: The dragon looked so real in 3D that I moved back in my seat.
cinema.item.action-film.s1: Action films have lots of car chases and fights.
cinema.item.actor.s2: The young actor who plays the hero is brilliant.
cinema.item.aisle.s1: Can I have a seat next to the aisle?
cinema.item.aisle.s2: I prefer an aisle seat so I can get out easily.
cinema.item.author.s1: She's my favourite author. I've read all her books.
cinema.item.author.s2: The author got the idea for the book on a long train journey.
cinema.item.bookmark.s1: I use a bookmark so I don't lose my page.
cinema.item.bookmark.s2: The library gives every new member a free bookmark.
cinema.item.boring.note: boring = the film; bored = how you feel.
cinema.item.boring.s3: The middle part dragged on a bit
cinema.item.borrow.note: You borrow FROM the library; the library lends TO you.
cinema.item.borrow.s1: How many books can I borrow?
cinema.item.borrow.s2: You can borrow up to five books for three weeks.
cinema.item.box-office.note: The desk where you buy tickets (also: ticket office).
cinema.item.box-office.s0: Buy tickets at the box office.
cinema.item.box-office.s1: The box office opens at ten in the morning.
cinema.item.box-office.s2: The film was a big success at the box office.
cinema.item.cartoon.note: Also: an animated film, an animation.
cinema.item.cartoon.s1: This cartoon is good for children and adults.
cinema.item.cartoon.s2: Animated films can take four or five years to make.
cinema.item.chapter.s0: I read one chapter every night.
cinema.item.chapter.s1: The first chapter is a bit slow
cinema.item.chapter.s2: Each chapter ends with a question
cinema.item.character.s0: The main character is a cat.
cinema.item.character.s1: My favourite character is the funny robot.
cinema.item.character.s2: The characters feel real because they make mistakes like us.
cinema.item.comedy.s1: Let's watch a comedy tonight. I want to laugh.
cinema.item.comedy.s2: The comedy was so funny that the whole cinema was laughing.
cinema.item.director.s1: The director also wrote the story.
cinema.item.documentary.s0: We watch a documentary about whales.
cinema.item.documentary.s1: Documentaries tell true stories about real people and places.
cinema.item.documentary.s2: I learned a lot from that documentary about the ocean.
cinema.item.due-date.s1: When is the due date for this book?
cinema.item.due-date.s2: If you return a book after the due date
cinema.item.ending.s1: The film has a happy ending.
cinema.item.ending.s2: Don't tell me the ending! I haven't seen it yet.
cinema.item.exciting.s2: The film was exciting from start to finish
cinema.item.exciting.s3: It's one of the most exciting films I've seen this year.
cinema.item.fantasy.s0: There are dragons in fantasy films.
cinema.item.fantasy.s1: She reads fantasy books about magic and wizards.
cinema.item.fantasy.s2: The fantasy world in the film looks completely real.
cinema.item.funny.s1: It's the funniest film I've ever seen!
cinema.item.funny.s2: The jokes were funny for adults and children.
cinema.item.horror-film.s1: Horror films are too scary for young children.
cinema.item.horror-film.s2: I watched the horror film with my hands over my eyes!
cinema.item.ice-cream.s1: Do you have chocolate ice cream?
cinema.item.ice-cream.s2: Eat your ice cream quickly or it'll melt before the film starts.
cinema.item.library-card.s1: You need a library card to borrow books.
cinema.item.library-card.s2: Getting a library card is free; you just need to fill in a form.
cinema.item.musical.s1: We went to see a musical and sang all the way home.
cinema.item.musical.s2: The songs in the musical are still stuck in my head.
cinema.item.nachos.s2: The nachos come with cheese sauce and a little salsa.
cinema.item.novel.s1: This novel is about a boy and his dog.
cinema.item.novel.s2: The novel was made into a film last year.
cinema.item.plot.s1: The plot is about a girl who finds a magic key.
cinema.item.plot.s2: The plot was so complicated that I had to watch it twice.
cinema.item.popcorn.note: Uncountable: some popcorn, a box of popcorn. Small $4, large $6.
cinema.item.popcorn.s1: A large popcorn and two drinks
cinema.item.popcorn.s2: Would you like sweet or salted popcorn?
cinema.item.recommend.s1: Can you recommend a good book for a twelve-year-old?
cinema.item.recommend.s2: I'd highly recommend it to anyone who loves a good mystery.
cinema.item.return.s1: Please return the books by Friday.
cinema.item.return.s2: You can return books in the box outside when the library is closed.
cinema.item.review.s1: I read a review before I choose a film.
cinema.item.review.s2: The critics gave it mixed reviews
cinema.item.row.s1: I don't like sitting in the front row.
cinema.item.row.s2: The seats in the back row have the best view of the screen.
cinema.item.sad.s1: I cried at the end because it was so sad.
cinema.item.sad.s3: The ending was so moving that half the audience was in tears.
cinema.item.scary.s1: Is this film too scary for children?
cinema.item.science-fiction.note: Short: sci-fi. Uncountable: a science fiction film.
cinema.item.science-fiction.s1: It's a science fiction film about robots on Mars.
cinema.item.science-fiction.s2: Good science fiction makes you think about the future.
cinema.item.screen.s1: The film is on screen two.
cinema.item.screen.s2: Please turn off your phone before the film starts on the big screen.
cinema.item.seat.s1: Can we have two seats next to each other?
cinema.item.seat.s2: Excuse me, I think you're sitting in my seat.
cinema.item.showtime.note: Also: a show, a screening. The 7:30 show.
cinema.item.showtime.s0: The film is at seven thirty.
cinema.item.showtime.s1: What are the showtimes for Space Cats?
cinema.item.showtime.s2: The evening showtimes are usually busier than the afternoon ones.
cinema.item.soft-drink.s2: You can refill your soft drink for free during the film.
cinema.item.subtitles.s1: I watch English films with English subtitles.
cinema.item.subtitles.s2: Reading subtitles is a great way to learn new words.
cinema.item.surprising.s1: The ending was surprising. I didn't expect it!
cinema.item.surprising.s2: The most surprising thing was that the villain was the hero's brother.
cinema.item.surprising.s3: I never saw that twist coming
cinema.item.ticket.s1: How much is a ticket for a child?
cinema.item.ticket.s2: It's cheaper to book your tickets online in advance.
cinema.item.trailer.s1: The trailer for that film looks really exciting.
cinema.item.trailer.s2: There are about fifteen minutes of trailers before the film starts.
cinema.phrase.0: Two tickets for Space Cats, please.
cinema.phrase.1: What time does the film start?
cinema.phrase.10: What did you think of the film?
cinema.phrase.11: I loved it! It was really exciting.
cinema.phrase.12: It was OK, but the ending was a bit disappointing.
cinema.phrase.13: In my opinion, the book was better than the film.
cinema.phrase.14: I'd recommend it to anyone who likes adventure stories.
cinema.phrase.15: I'm not really into horror films.
cinema.phrase.16: I'd like to borrow this book, please.
cinema.phrase.17: When do I have to return it?
cinema.phrase.18: Do you have any books by this author?
cinema.phrase.19: Can I renew it for another week?
cinema.phrase.2: Are there any seats left for the 7:30 show?
cinema.phrase.20: It's due back on the twenty-first.
cinema.phrase.21: It's about a girl who can talk to animals.
cinema.phrase.22: The main character is a shy boy called Tom.
cinema.phrase.23: It's set in a small town by the sea.
cinema.phrase.24: At first she's scared, but in the end she saves her friends.
cinema.phrase.25: Without giving away the ending, it's full of surprises.
cinema.phrase.3: Can we sit next to each other?
cinema.phrase.4: One adult and one child, please.
cinema.phrase.8: Can I have a small drink with no ice?
cinema.title: Star Cinema & Library
clothes.intro: Come into the shop, find clothes in your favourite colours and try them on in the fitting room. Learn the names of clothes, sizes and what to say when you shop.
clothes.item.backpack.s1: I carry my books in my backpack.
clothes.item.backpack.s2: This backpack has a pocket for a water bottle on each side.
clothes.item.beanie.s1: I wear a beanie in winter.
clothes.item.beanie.s2: You lose a lot of heat through your head, so a beanie really helps.
clothes.item.belt.s1: My trousers are too big. I need a belt.
clothes.item.belt.s2: A leather belt goes well with smart shoes.
clothes.item.boots.s0: I wear boots in the rain.
clothes.item.boots.s1: These brown boots are made of leather.
clothes.item.boots.s2: Walking boots should feel comfortable before you go on a long hike.
clothes.item.cap.s1: A cap keeps the sun out of your eyes.
clothes.item.cap.s2: Some people wear their caps backwards.
clothes.item.checked.note: with squares, like a chessboard (Americans say plaid or checkered)
clothes.item.checked.s1: A checked skirt is part of my uniform.
clothes.item.checked.s2: Checked shirts are popular with people who work outdoors.
clothes.item.coat.s1: My winter coat is long and black.
clothes.item.coat.s2: This coat is waterproof, so you won't get wet in the rain.
clothes.item.cotton.note: Uncountable. A soft material made from a plant.
clothes.item.cotton.s2: Cotton clothes are easy to wash, but they crease easily.
clothes.item.dress.s1: I'd like a blue dress, size M, please.
clothes.item.dress.s2: She's looking for a dress to wear to her cousin's wedding.
clothes.item.fit.note: It fits = it's the right size. It suits you = it looks good on you.
clothes.item.fit.s1: The jacket doesn't fit. It's too big.
clothes.item.fit.s2: The jeans fit me perfectly, and the colour suits me too.
clothes.item.fitting-room.note: The small room where you try clothes on. Americans say dressing room.
clothes.item.fitting-room.s1: You can take three items into the fitting room.
clothes.item.fitting-room.s2: There was a long queue for the fitting rooms because of the sale.
clothes.item.glasses.note: Always plural: a pair of glasses.
clothes.item.glasses.s1: I need my glasses to read.
clothes.item.glasses.s2: These round glasses really suit you.
clothes.item.hoodie.note: A warm top with a hood.
clothes.item.hoodie.s1: Can I try on the red hoodie?
clothes.item.hoodie.s2: I always wear a hoodie when it's windy, because I can put the hood up.
clothes.item.jacket.s1: This jacket has two big pockets.
clothes.item.jacket.s2: A light jacket is perfect for a cool spring evening.
clothes.item.jeans.note: Always plural: a pair of jeans.
clothes.item.jeans.s1: These jeans are too tight. Can I have a bigger size?
clothes.item.leather.note: Uncountable. Shoes, belts and bags are often leather.
clothes.item.leather.s2: Leather lasts for years if you clean it regularly.
clothes.item.loose.s1: This shirt is too loose. Do you have a smaller one?
clothes.item.loose.s2: Loose clothes keep you cool when the weather is hot and humid.
clothes.item.mirror.s1: There's a big mirror next to the fitting rooms.
clothes.item.mirror.s2: I looked in the mirror and decided the colour didn't suit me.
clothes.item.on-sale.note: cheaper than usual for a short time
clothes.item.on-sale.s1: Everything is half price in the sale this week.
clothes.item.on-sale.s2: It was on sale, so I got it for half the normal price.
clothes.item.overalls.note: Trousers with a top part and straps. Always plural: a pair of overalls.
clothes.item.overalls.s1: Overalls have a big pocket on the front.
clothes.item.overalls.s2: Overalls were work clothes, but now they're fashionable too.
clothes.item.price-tag.s1: There's no price tag on this hat. How much is it?
clothes.item.price-tag.s2: Don't take the price tags off until you're sure you want to keep it.
clothes.item.receipt.s1: Keep the receipt if you want to change it.
clothes.item.receipt.s2: You can return anything within 30 days, as long as you have the receipt.
clothes.item.sandals.s0: I wear sandals on the beach.
clothes.item.sandals.s1: These sandals are cheap and comfortable.
clothes.item.sandals.s2: You can't wear sandals in the science lab for safety reasons.
clothes.item.scarf.s1: Wear a scarf. It's very cold today.
clothes.item.scarf.s2: This scarf is made of soft wool, so it isn't itchy.
clothes.item.shirt.note: A shirt has buttons and a collar.
clothes.item.shirt.s0: Dad is wearing a white shirt.
clothes.item.shirt.s1: I need a shirt for school.
clothes.item.shirt.s2: This shirt needs ironing, so it's a bit creased.
clothes.item.shoes.s1: What size are your shoes? — I'm a size 38.
clothes.item.shoes.s2: These shoes look great, but they hurt my feet a little.
clothes.item.shorts.note: Always plural: a pair of shorts.
clothes.item.shorts.s2: Shorts aren't allowed at some temples, so bring long trousers.
clothes.item.size.note: Sizes: S (small), M (medium), L (large), XL (extra large).
clothes.item.size.s1: Do you have this in a large? — Sorry, we only have small and medium.
clothes.item.size.s2: Sizes are different in every shop, so always try things on first.
clothes.item.skirt.s1: She's wearing a long skirt today.
clothes.item.skirt.s2: A pleated skirt is part of the school uniform at many schools.
clothes.item.socks.s1: I need two pairs of white socks.
clothes.item.socks.s2: I can never find matching socks after I do the washing.
clothes.item.spotted.note: with round spots — also called polka dot
clothes.item.spotted.s0: The dress is red and spotted.
clothes.item.spotted.s2: Polka dots were very popular in the 1950s.
clothes.item.striped.s1: The sailor is wearing a blue and white striped shirt.
clothes.item.striped.s2: Vertical stripes can make you look taller.
clothes.item.suit.note: A jacket and trousers in the same colour.
clothes.item.suit.s0: He is wearing a black suit.
clothes.item.suit.s1: You need a suit for a job interview.
clothes.item.suit.s2: The suit fits well, but the trousers are a little long.
clothes.item.sun-hat.s0: Wear a sun hat at the beach.
clothes.item.sun-hat.s1: This sun hat has a wide brim.
clothes.item.sun-hat.s2: A sun hat protects your face and neck from sunburn.
clothes.item.sunglasses.note: Always plural: a pair of sunglasses.
clothes.item.sunglasses.s2: Good sunglasses protect your eyes from strong sunlight.
clothes.item.sweater.s1: Grandma made me a green sweater.
clothes.item.sweater.s2: Wool sweaters can shrink if you wash them in hot water.
clothes.item.t-shirt.s1: This T-shirt is too small. Do you have a medium?
clothes.item.t-shirt.s2: Cotton T-shirts are cool and comfortable in hot weather.
clothes.item.tie.s1: You wear a tie with a shirt and a suit.
clothes.item.tie.s2: Ties are less common at work now, except at formal events.
clothes.item.tight.s1: These shoes are too tight. I need a bigger size.
clothes.item.tight.s2: Tight clothes look smart, but loose ones are better for sport.
clothes.item.top-hat.s0: The magician has a top hat.
clothes.item.top-hat.s1: A top hat is tall and black.
clothes.item.top-hat.s2: Rich gentlemen wore top hats in the 1800s.
clothes.item.trainers.s1: Can I try these trainers in a size 40?
clothes.item.trainers.s2: Good trainers are expensive, but they're worth it if you run a lot.
clothes.item.trousers.note: Always plural: a pair of trousers. Americans say pants.
clothes.item.trousers.s1: I'd like a pair of black trousers.
clothes.item.trousers.s2: These trousers are too long, but they can shorten them for you.
clothes.item.try-on.note: try something on, try it on
clothes.item.try-on.s1: I tried on three dresses, but none of them fitted.
clothes.item.try-on.s2: You should try the shoes on with the socks you'll wear with them.
clothes.item.wool.s1: My scarf is made of wool.
clothes.item.wool.s2: Some people can't wear wool because it makes their skin itch.
clothes.phrase.10: Do you have this in red?
clothes.phrase.11: What other colours do you have?
clothes.phrase.12: I'd prefer something plain, without a pattern.
clothes.phrase.13: Which one goes better with my blue jeans?
clothes.phrase.17: I'd like to return these shoes. They're too small.
clothes.phrase.18: Could I change it for a bigger size?
clothes.phrase.20: You can get a refund or exchange it within 30 days.
clothes.phrase.23: You look great in that jacket.
clothes.phrase.24: Where did you get those trainers? They're really cool.
clothes.phrase.4: Excuse me, do you sell school uniforms?
clothes.phrase.7: It's too big. Do you have a smaller size?
clothes.phrase.8: These jeans are a bit tight around the waist.
clothes.title: Style Corner
farm.intro: Meet the farm animals, grow your own vegetables and sell them at the market. Every job on the farm teaches you an action word.
farm.item.apple.note: Apples grow on apple trees in an orchard.
farm.item.apple.s1: There are a lot of apples on the tree.
farm.item.apple.s2: The apples fell off the tree in the strong wind.
farm.item.barn.s0: The barn is big and red.
farm.item.barn.s1: The cows sleep in the barn at night.
farm.item.barn.s2: The farmer stores the tractor and the hay in the barn.
farm.item.bucket.s0: The bucket is full of water.
farm.item.bucket.s1: Can you carry this bucket to the pigs?
farm.item.bucket.s2: We use a bucket to bring food to the animals.
farm.item.carrot.s1: The carrots are ready to pick.
farm.item.carrot.s2: Carrots grow best in soft, sandy soil.
farm.item.chicken.fact: A hen can lay about 300 eggs a year.
farm.item.chicken.note: The chicken says cluck. A female chicken is a hen.
farm.item.chicken.s1: The hens lay eggs every day.
farm.item.chicken.s2: The chickens are kept in a coop at night.
farm.item.collect-eggs.s1: We collected twelve eggs this morning.
farm.item.collect-eggs.s2: The eggs must be collected carefully so they don't break.
farm.item.corn.note: Uncountable: some corn, an ear of corn.
farm.item.corn.s1: The corn grows very tall in summer.
farm.item.corn.s2: Popcorn is made from a special kind of corn.
farm.item.cow.fact: A cow can give about 30 litres of milk a day.
farm.item.cow.s2: The farmer milks the cows every morning.
farm.item.dig.s1: We dug up the potatoes yesterday.
farm.item.dig.s2: The ground was so hard that it took hours to dig.
farm.item.donkey.fact: Donkeys have very long ears to hear far away.
farm.item.donkey.s1: The donkey is carrying a heavy bag.
farm.item.donkey.s2: Donkeys are famous for being stubborn.
farm.item.egg.s1: The hens laid six eggs today.
farm.item.egg.s2: Fresh eggs sink in water, but old ones float.
farm.item.farmer.s1: The farmer gets up very early every day.
farm.item.farmer.s2: Farmers have to check the weather before they decide what to do.
farm.item.feed.s1: The farmer fed the pigs an hour ago.
farm.item.feed.s2: The animals are fed twice a day.
farm.item.fence.s0: The fence is made of wood.
farm.item.fence.s1: The sheep can't jump over the fence.
farm.item.fence.s2: Please close the gate in the fence, or the goats will get out.
farm.item.field.s0: The cows are in the field.
farm.item.field.s1: There is a field of corn behind the barn.
farm.item.field.s2: The farmer lets one field rest every few years so the soil stays healthy.
farm.item.goat.note: A baby goat is called a kid.
farm.item.goat.s1: The goat is climbing on a rock.
farm.item.goat.s2: Goats will try to eat almost anything.
farm.item.harvest.s1: We harvested a lot of corn this year.
farm.item.harvest.s2: The harvest was smaller because of the dry summer.
farm.item.hay.note: Uncountable: some hay, a bale of hay.
farm.item.hay.s1: We keep the hay in the barn.
farm.item.hay.s2: Hay is dried grass that animals eat in winter.
farm.item.honey.s1: The bees make honey in the hive.
farm.item.honey.s2: Honey never goes bad if you keep it in a closed jar.
farm.item.horse.s2: The horse is used to pull the old cart.
farm.item.milk.note: Also a noun: a glass of milk.
farm.item.milk.s1: Have you ever milked a cow?
farm.item.milk.s2: Cows are usually milked early in the morning.
farm.item.orchard.s0: There are apple trees in the orchard.
farm.item.orchard.s1: We picked pears in the orchard.
farm.item.orchard.s2: In spring, the orchard is full of white and pink flowers.
farm.item.pick.s2: The cherries should be picked as soon as they are red.
farm.item.pig.fact: Pigs roll in mud to stay cool.
farm.item.pig.s1: The pigs are playing in the mud.
farm.item.pig.s2: Pigs are cleverer than most people think.
farm.item.plant.s2: Seeds should be planted in spring.
farm.item.potato.s1: We dig the potatoes out of the ground.
farm.item.potato.s2: Potatoes can be boiled, fried or baked.
farm.item.pumpkin.s0: The pumpkin is big and orange.
farm.item.pumpkin.s1: This pumpkin is heavier than that one.
farm.item.pumpkin.s2: People carve faces into pumpkins at Halloween.
farm.item.ride.s1: Have you ever ridden a donkey?
farm.item.ride.s2: She learned to ride when she was only five years old.
farm.item.scarecrow.s0: The scarecrow has a big hat.
farm.item.scarecrow.s1: The scarecrow stands in the middle of the field.
farm.item.scarecrow.s2: A scarecrow is used to frighten birds away from the crops.
farm.item.seed.s1: Put the seeds in the ground and water them.
farm.item.seed.s2: Each seed needs sun, water and good soil to grow.
farm.item.sheep.fact: Wool for sweaters comes from sheep.
farm.item.sheep.note: The sheep says baa. One sheep, two sheep!
farm.item.sheep.s0: The sheep is white and soft.
farm.item.sheep.s1: There are ten sheep in the field.
farm.item.sheep.s2: Sheep are usually sheared once a year.
farm.item.strawberry.s2: Strawberries are the only fruit with seeds on the outside.
farm.item.tomato.s1: We need tomatoes for the salad.
farm.item.tomato.s2: Tomatoes need a lot of sun and water.
farm.item.tractor.s1: The farmer drives the tractor to the field.
farm.item.tractor.s2: A tractor can pull much heavier loads than a horse.
farm.item.water.s1: Don't forget to water the tomatoes.
farm.item.water.s2: The plants have been watered twice today.
farm.item.wheat.s1: The farmer harvests the wheat in autumn.
farm.item.wheat.s2: The wheat is ground into flour at the mill.
farm.item.wool.s1: My grandma made this sweater from wool.
farm.item.wool.s2: The wool is washed and spun into yarn before it is used.
farm.phrase.11: Could I have a bag of potatoes, please?
farm.phrase.12: It's sunny today. The plants will grow fast.
farm.phrase.13: We need rain. The ground is very dry.
farm.phrase.14: In autumn we harvest the apples.
farm.phrase.15: Let's drive the tractor to the field.
farm.phrase.16: Put the hay in the barn, please.
farm.phrase.17: The baby sheep is called a lamb.
farm.phrase.18: Do you sell fresh eggs and honey?
farm.phrase.3: Be careful, the horse might kick.
farm.phrase.6: When will the pumpkins be ready?
farm.phrase.7: Can you help me harvest the corn?
farm.title: Green Valley Farm
home.intro: Welcome to Cozy Home! Look around the rooms, learn the names of things in the house and help Mum with the chores.
home.item.ball.s0: The ball is under the bed.
home.item.ball.s1: Don't play with the ball in the house!
home.item.ball.s2: I kicked the ball so hard that it went over the fence.
home.item.bath.s0: The duck is in the bath.
home.item.bath.s1: The baby has a bath every evening.
home.item.bath.s2: I'd rather have a quick shower than a long bath.
home.item.bathroom.s0: The bathroom is next to my bedroom.
home.item.bathroom.s1: I have a shower in the bathroom every morning.
home.item.bathroom.s2: Please don't leave wet towels on the bathroom floor.
home.item.bed.s0: The ball is under the bed.
home.item.bed.s1: I make my bed every morning.
home.item.bed.s2: I was so tired that I went straight to bed after dinner.
home.item.bedroom.s0: My bedroom is small and blue.
home.item.bedroom.s1: I sleep and do my homework in my bedroom.
home.item.bedroom.s2: I share a bedroom with my little brother, so we have bunk beds.
home.item.bookcase.s0: The books are in the bookcase.
home.item.bookcase.s1: There are lots of picture books on the bottom shelf.
home.item.bookcase.s2: We sorted the books in the bookcase by colour.
home.item.bowl.s0: I have a bowl of rice.
home.item.bowl.s1: Put the bowls on the table, please.
home.item.bowl.s2: I eat a bowl of cereal with milk before school.
home.item.brush-my-teeth.s0: I brush my teeth in the morning.
home.item.brush-my-teeth.s1: I brush my teeth twice a day.
home.item.brush-my-teeth.s2: I always brush my teeth before bed, even when I'm really tired.
home.item.chair.s1: There are four chairs around the table.
home.item.chair.s2: Can you put the chairs back when you've finished eating?
home.item.clock.s0: The clock is on the wall.
home.item.clock.s1: Look at the clock. It's seven o'clock!
home.item.clock.s2: The kitchen clock is five minutes fast, so we're never late.
home.item.cooker.s0: The pan is on the cooker.
home.item.cooker.s1: Be careful! The cooker is hot.
home.item.cooker.s2: Never leave the cooker on when you go out.
home.item.cup.s1: Would you like a cup of tea?
home.item.cup.s2: I dropped a cup this morning and it broke into pieces.
home.item.cupboard.note: Say it like “CUB-bud”: the p is silent.
home.item.cupboard.s0: The plates are in the cupboard.
home.item.cupboard.s1: Can you put the cups in the cupboard, please?
home.item.cupboard.s2: The biscuits are in the top cupboard, where the baby can't reach them.
home.item.desk.s0: My books are on my desk.
home.item.desk.s1: I do my homework at my desk.
home.item.desk.s2: I keep my desk tidy so I can find my pens quickly.
home.item.do-my-homework.s0: I do my homework after school.
home.item.do-my-homework.s1: I do my homework at my desk before dinner.
home.item.do-my-homework.s2: I can't watch TV until I've finished my homework.
home.item.do-the-washing.note: In American English: do the laundry.
home.item.do-the-washing.s0: Mum does the washing on Saturday.
home.item.do-the-washing.s1: Put your dirty socks in the basket, then I can do the washing.
home.item.do-the-washing.s2: It's raining, so we'll have to dry the washing inside.
home.item.door.s1: Someone is knocking at the front door.
home.item.door.s2: Don't forget to lock the door when you go out.
home.item.fridge.s0: The milk is in the fridge.
home.item.fridge.s1: Put the butter back in the fridge, please.
home.item.fridge.s2: There's nothing in the fridge, so we need to go shopping.
home.item.garden.note: In American English people often say “yard”.
home.item.garden.s0: There are flowers in the garden.
home.item.garden.s1: The children are playing in the garden.
home.item.garden.s2: Mum hangs the washing on the line in the garden when it's sunny.
home.item.get-up.s0: I get up at six o'clock.
home.item.get-up.s1: What time do you get up on Sundays?
home.item.get-up.s2: I find it really hard to get up when it's cold and dark.
home.item.go-to-bed.s0: I go to bed at nine o'clock.
home.item.go-to-bed.s1: What time do you go to bed?
home.item.go-to-bed.s2: I went to bed late last night, so I'm a bit sleepy today.
home.item.go-to-school.s0: I go to school by bus.
home.item.go-to-school.s1: I go to school at half past seven.
home.item.go-to-school.s2: When it's sunny, I walk to school with my friends.
home.item.have-breakfast.s0: I have breakfast at seven o'clock.
home.item.have-breakfast.s1: I usually have bread and an egg for breakfast.
home.item.have-breakfast.s2: If I don't have breakfast, I feel hungry all morning.
home.item.have-dinner.s0: We have dinner at seven o'clock.
home.item.have-dinner.s1: My family has dinner together every evening.
home.item.have-dinner.s2: While we're having dinner, we talk about our day.
home.item.house.s1: Our house has four rooms and a small garden.
home.item.house.s2: We've lived in this house since I was a baby.
home.item.keys.s1: The keys are next to the door.
home.item.keys.s2: Dad always loses his keys, so we hang them on a hook by the door.
home.item.kitchen.s1: We cook and wash the dishes in the kitchen.
home.item.kitchen.s2: The kitchen always smells nice when Dad is baking bread.
home.item.lamp.s0: The lamp is on the desk.
home.item.lamp.s1: Turn on the lamp. It's dark in here.
home.item.lamp.s2: Please switch off the lamp when you leave the room to save electricity.
home.item.living-room.s0: The sofa is in the living room.
home.item.living-room.s1: We watch TV in the living room in the evening.
home.item.living-room.s2: The living room is the biggest room in our house.
home.item.make-the-bed.s0: I make my bed every day.
home.item.make-the-bed.s1: Don't forget to make your bed before school.
home.item.make-the-bed.s2: My room looks much tidier when I've made the bed.
home.item.mirror.s1: There's a mirror above the sink in the bathroom.
home.item.mirror.s2: I checked my hair in the mirror before I went out.
home.item.plant.s1: Please water the plants in the living room.
home.item.plant.s2: The plant grew so tall that we had to move it outside.
home.item.sink.s0: The cups are in the sink.
home.item.sink.s1: I wash my hands at the kitchen sink.
home.item.sink.s2: The sink is full of dirty dishes after the party.
home.item.soap.note: Uncountable: some soap, a bar of soap.
home.item.soap.s1: There's no soap in the bathroom. Can you get some?
home.item.soap.s2: Washing your hands with soap for twenty seconds kills most germs.
home.item.sofa.s0: The cat is on the sofa.
home.item.sofa.s1: We sit on the sofa and read stories.
home.item.sofa.s2: The sofa is so comfortable that Grandpa often falls asleep on it.
home.item.sweep-the-floor.s1: Can you sweep the kitchen floor, please?
home.item.sweep-the-floor.s2: We need to sweep the floor because there are crumbs everywhere.
home.item.table.s0: The plates are on the table.
home.item.table.s1: We have dinner at the big table in the dining room.
home.item.table.s2: It's your turn to lay the table tonight.
home.item.take-out-the-rubbish.note: In American English: take out the trash.
home.item.take-out-the-rubbish.s0: My brother takes out the rubbish.
home.item.take-out-the-rubbish.s1: The bin is full. Please take out the rubbish.
home.item.take-out-the-rubbish.s2: We take out the rubbish on Tuesday night because it's collected on Wednesday.
home.item.teddy-bear.s0: My teddy bear is on my bed.
home.item.teddy-bear.s1: My little sister can't sleep without her teddy bear.
home.item.teddy-bear.s2: I've had this teddy bear since I was two years old.
home.item.toilet.s1: The toilet is next to the bath.
home.item.toilet.s2: Remember to flush the toilet and wash your hands.
home.item.toothbrush.s1: The toothbrushes are in a cup next to the sink.
home.item.toothbrush.s2: Dentists say you should get a new toothbrush every three months.
home.item.wardrobe.s0: My clothes are in the wardrobe.
home.item.wardrobe.s1: Hang your coat in the wardrobe, please.
home.item.wardrobe.s2: The wardrobe is so full that the door won't close.
home.item.wash-the-dishes.s0: I wash the dishes after dinner.
home.item.wash-the-dishes.s1: Can you help me wash the dishes, please?
home.item.wash-the-dishes.s2: If you cook, I'll wash the dishes.
home.item.water-the-plants.s0: I water the plants on Sunday.

home.item.water-the-plants.s2: Could you water the plants while we're on holiday?
home.item.window.s1: I can see the garden from my bedroom window.
home.item.window.s2: It's cold in here because somebody left the window open.
home.phrase.1: Welcome home! How was your day?

hospital.intro: Welcome to City Hospital! Learn the parts of the body, say how you feel and help the pharmacist give every patient the right medicine.
hospital.item.after-meals.s1: Take one tablet three times a day after meals.
hospital.item.ambulance.s1: Call an ambulance! He has hurt his head.
hospital.item.ambulance.s2: Only call an ambulance in an emergency
hospital.item.appointment.s0: I have an appointment at ten.
hospital.item.appointment.s1: I'd like to make an appointment with the doctor.
hospital.item.arm.s1: He broke his arm playing football.
hospital.item.arm.s2: The nurse put a bandage round my arm to stop the bleeding.
hospital.item.back.s1: Don't carry heavy bags or you'll hurt your back.
hospital.item.back.s2: Sitting up straight at your desk is good for your back.
hospital.item.bandage.s1: Wrap a bandage round your ankle.
hospital.item.cough-syrup.note: A sweet liquid medicine. You take it with a spoon.
hospital.item.cough-syrup.s1: Take two spoons of cough syrup three times a day.
hospital.item.cough-syrup.s2: Cough syrup can make you sleepy
hospital.item.cough.note: Also a verb – "He coughs a lot at night."
hospital.item.cough.s1: My cough is worse at night.
hospital.item.cough.s2: A dry cough can last for a few weeks after a cold.
hospital.item.cream.s1: Put this cream on the rash twice a day.
hospital.item.cream.s2: Rub the cream in gently and wash your hands afterwards.
hospital.item.cut.s0: I have a cut on my finger.
hospital.item.cut.s1: Clean the cut and put a plaster on it.
hospital.item.cut.s2: A small cut usually heals in a few days if you keep it clean.
hospital.item.dizzy.s1: Sit down if you feel dizzy.
hospital.item.dizzy.s2: Standing in the hot sun for too long can make you feel dizzy.
hospital.item.drink-water.s2: Drinking plenty of water helps your body fight the illness.
hospital.item.ear-drops.s1: Put three ear drops in the ear that hurts
hospital.item.ear-drops.s2: Warm the bottle in your hand first
hospital.item.ear.s2: Don't put anything in your ear; ask a doctor to look at it.
hospital.item.earache.s1: Children often get an earache after a cold.
hospital.item.earache.s2: Swimming in dirty water can sometimes give you an earache.
hospital.item.eye-drops.s1: Put two eye drops in each eye in the morning and evening.
hospital.item.eye-drops.s2: Don't wear contact lenses while you are using these eye drops.
hospital.item.eye.s1: My eyes are red and itchy.
hospital.item.eye.s2: Rest your eyes for a few minutes every hour if you work on a computer.
hospital.item.fever.note: In British English you also hear "a temperature" – "I've got a temperature."
hospital.item.fever.s1: He has a fever of 38.5 degrees.
hospital.item.fever.s2: If the fever lasts more than three days
hospital.item.foot.s1: These new shoes hurt my feet.
hospital.item.foot.s2: After walking all day at the zoo
hospital.item.for-five-days.s1: Use the eye drops for five days
hospital.item.hand.s1: I cut my hand on some glass.
hospital.item.hand.s2: Washing your hands often is the easiest way to stop colds from spreading.
hospital.item.head.s1: I hit my head on the door.
hospital.item.head.s2: Wear a helmet to protect your head when you ride a bike.
hospital.item.headache.s1: I've had a headache since this morning.
hospital.item.headache.s2: Too much screen time and not enough water can give you a headache.
hospital.item.ice-pack.s1: Put an ice pack on your ankle for twenty minutes.
hospital.item.ice-pack.s2: Wrap the ice pack in a towel so it doesn't hurt your skin.
hospital.item.insect-bite.s1: The mosquito bites on my legs are very itchy.
hospital.item.insect-bite.s2: Try not to scratch an insect bite
hospital.item.knee.s0: I fell and hurt my knee.
hospital.item.knee.s1: Put a plaster on your knee.
hospital.item.knee.s2: Running on hard roads can be bad for your knees.
hospital.item.leg.s1: My legs are tired after the run.
hospital.item.leg.s2: Stretch your legs before and after sport to avoid injuries.
hospital.item.mouth.s1: Cover your mouth when you cough.
hospital.item.mouth.s2: The dentist looked inside my mouth and found a small hole in a tooth.
hospital.item.neck.s0: The giraffe has a long neck.
hospital.item.neck.s1: My neck is stiff this morning.
hospital.item.neck.s2: Sleeping on a bad pillow can give you a sore neck.
hospital.item.nose.s1: I have a cold and my nose is blocked.
hospital.item.nose.s2: Breathe in slowly through your nose and out through your mouth.
hospital.item.nurse.s2: Nurses work long shifts and look after patients day and night.
hospital.item.pharmacy.note: In British English also "chemist's"; in the US also "drugstore".
hospital.item.pharmacy.s1: You can buy cough syrup at the pharmacy.
hospital.item.pharmacy.s2: The pharmacist can give you advice about small problems
hospital.item.plaster.note: In the US people say "Band-Aid" or "bandage".
hospital.item.plaster.s1: Put a plaster on your cut.
hospital.item.plaster.s2: Change the plaster every day and keep the cut dry.
hospital.item.prescription.s1: You need a prescription from the doctor for this medicine.
hospital.item.prescription.s2: Bring your prescription to the pharmacy and they will prepare your medicine.
hospital.item.rash.s0: I have a rash on my arm.
hospital.item.rash.s1: The rash is red and very itchy.
hospital.item.rash.s2: Some people get a rash when they eat nuts or strawberries.
hospital.item.reception.s1: Give your name at reception and take a seat.
hospital.item.reception.s2: The nurse at reception will ask you a few questions about your symptoms.
hospital.item.rest.s1: Stay at home and rest for two days.
hospital.item.rest.s2: Your body gets better faster if you rest and sleep well.
hospital.item.runny-nose.s1: I need tissues because I've got a runny nose.
hospital.item.runny-nose.s2: A runny nose and sneezing in spring may be an allergy
hospital.item.sore-throat.s1: It hurts when I swallow because I've got a sore throat.
hospital.item.sore-throat.s2: A sore throat is often the first sign of a cold.
hospital.item.sprained-ankle.s1: I fell during the match and sprained my ankle.
hospital.item.sprained-ankle.s2: With a sprained ankle you should keep your foot up and put ice on it.
hospital.item.stomach-ache.s1: I've got a stomach ache because I ate too fast.
hospital.item.stomach-ache.s2: If you have a stomach ache
hospital.item.stomach.s1: I ate too much and now my stomach hurts.
hospital.item.stomach.s2: Take these tablets on a full stomach
hospital.item.tablet.note: Also called "pills". Swallow them with water.
hospital.item.tablet.s1: Take two tablets with a glass of water.
hospital.item.tablet.s2: Don't take more than eight tablets in twenty-four hours.
hospital.item.thermometer.s1: Use the thermometer to check your temperature.
hospital.item.thermometer.s2: A normal body temperature is about 37 degrees
hospital.item.throat-lozenges.note: Small sweets for a sore throat. Let them melt in your mouth – don't chew them.
hospital.item.throat-lozenges.s0: These throat lozenges taste of honey.
hospital.item.throat-lozenges.s1: Suck one throat lozenge every three hours.
hospital.item.throat-lozenges.s2: Throat lozenges help with the pain
hospital.item.throat.s1: Drink something warm for your throat.
hospital.item.throat.s2: Singers have to look after their throats
hospital.item.tooth.s1: My tooth hurts when I eat ice cream.
hospital.item.tooth.s2: Eating too many sweets is bad for your teeth.
hospital.item.toothache.s1: You should see a dentist about your toothache.
hospital.item.toothache.s2: The toothache was so bad that I couldn't sleep all night.
hospital.item.twice-a-day.note: once a day = 1 time, twice a day = 2 times, three times a day = 3 times
hospital.item.twice-a-day.s1: Use the cream twice a day
hospital.item.ward.s0: My grandma is in the ward.
hospital.item.ward.s1: The children's ward is on the second floor.
hospital.item.ward.s2: Visitors can come to the ward between two and eight in the afternoon.
hospital.phrase.1: I've got a headache and a sore throat.
hospital.phrase.10: How often should I take it?
hospital.phrase.11: Take two tablets three times a day after meals.
hospital.phrase.12: Take two spoons of syrup before bed.
hospital.phrase.14: Don't take more than eight tablets a day.
hospital.phrase.15: You should rest and drink plenty of water.
hospital.phrase.16: You shouldn't go to school today.
hospital.phrase.17: Put some ice on it and keep your foot up.
hospital.phrase.18: If it doesn't get better, see a doctor.
hospital.phrase.19: I hope you feel better soon!
hospital.phrase.2: My ankle hurts when I walk.
hospital.phrase.21: The waiting room is on the left.
hospital.phrase.22: Please take a seat. The nurse will call your name.
hospital.phrase.23: Which ward is my grandmother in?
hospital.phrase.3: I've had a cough for three days.
hospital.phrase.5: Have you got anything for a cough?
hospital.phrase.6: Can I buy this without a prescription?
hospital.phrase.8: I'd like a box of plasters, please.

hotel.intro: Check in at the front desk, book a room for your family and ask for help when something in your room doesn't work. Learn hotel words, dates and polite requests.
hotel.item.air-conditioner.s2: The air conditioner is making a strange noise all night.
hotel.item.balcony.s1: We had breakfast on the balcony.
hotel.item.balcony.s2: From the balcony, you can watch the boats on the river.
hotel.item.book.note: book a room, book a table: arrange it before you go
hotel.item.book.s0: I want to book a room.
hotel.item.book.s1: I booked a double room for three nights.
hotel.item.book.s2: It's a busy weekend, so you should book well in advance.
hotel.item.breakfast.s1: Is breakfast included in the price?
hotel.item.breakfast.s2: Breakfast is served in the restaurant on the ground floor until ten.
hotel.item.change-rooms.s1: We changed rooms because ours was too cold.
hotel.item.change-rooms.s2: Would it be possible to change rooms? Mine faces the busy road.
hotel.item.check-in.note: verb: check in · noun: check-in (Check-in is from 2 pm.)
hotel.item.check-in.s0: I'd like to check in, please.
hotel.item.check-in.s1: You can check in from two o'clock.
hotel.item.check-in.s2: If we arrive early, is it possible to check in before noon?
hotel.item.check-out.note: verb: check out · noun: check-out (Check-out is at 11 am.)
hotel.item.check-out.s1: What time do we have to check out?
hotel.item.check-out.s2: Could we check out a bit later? Our train leaves at four.
hotel.item.complain.note: complain about something; the noun is "complaint"
hotel.item.complain.s0: I don't want to complain, but…
hotel.item.complain.s2: If you complain politely, the staff are usually happy to help.
hotel.item.date.s1: What dates would you like to stay?
hotel.item.date.s2: Could you check the dates of my booking? I think there's a mistake.
hotel.item.deposit.s1: We need a deposit of fifty dollars.
hotel.item.deposit.s2: The deposit will be returned when you check out.
hotel.item.dirty.s1: The bathroom was dirty when we arrived.
hotel.item.dirty.s2: I'm sorry to say this, but the sheets don't look clean.
hotel.item.doesnt-work.s1: Sorry, the light in the bathroom doesn't work.
hotel.item.doesnt-work.s2: The safe doesn't work, so I can't lock my things away.
hotel.item.double-room.note: A room with one big bed for two people. $90 a night.
hotel.item.double-room.s0: We'd like a double room for two nights.
hotel.item.double-room.s1: The double room has a big bed and a balcony.
hotel.item.double-room.s2: Is there a double room available from the 14th of May?
hotel.item.family-room.note: A big room for two adults and two children. $140 a night.
hotel.item.family-room.s0: We need a family room for four people.
hotel.item.family-room.s1: The family room has a double bed and two single beds.
hotel.item.family-room.s2: Could we have a family room with a view of the river?
hotel.item.first.s0: Today is the first of June.
hotel.item.first.s1: We arrive on the 1st and leave on the 3rd.
hotel.item.first.s2: The first night is already paid for.
hotel.item.front-desk.s0: The front desk is open all night.
hotel.item.front-desk.s1: Please leave your key at the front desk.
hotel.item.front-desk.s2: If you need anything, just call the front desk by dialling zero.
hotel.item.full-name.note: first name + surname (family name): Kate Brown
hotel.item.full-name.s1: My full name is Kate Brown. That's B-R-O-W-N.
hotel.item.full-name.s2: Please write your full name in capital letters.
hotel.item.guest.s0: The hotel has many guests today.
hotel.item.guest.s1: Guests can use the pool for free.
hotel.item.guest.s2: The receptionist welcomed every guest with a smile.
hotel.item.hairdryer.s1: The hairdryer is in the bathroom drawer.
hotel.item.hairdryer.s2: Could you send up a hairdryer? Mine isn't working.
hotel.item.key-card.s1: Put the key card in the slot to turn on the lights.
hotel.item.key-card.s2: I've lost my key card. Could you give me a new one?
hotel.item.lift.s0: The lift is on the left.
hotel.item.lift.s1: Take the lift to the third floor.
hotel.item.lift.s2: The lift is out of order, so you'll have to use the stairs.
hotel.item.lost.s1: I've lost my key card. Can you help me?
hotel.item.lost.s2: Someone found a lost umbrella in the lobby this morning.
hotel.item.luggage.note: uncountable: some luggage, a piece of luggage, two bags
hotel.item.luggage.s1: Can I leave my luggage here until five?
hotel.item.luggage.s2: The porter will take your luggage up to your room.
hotel.item.night.s0: I want to stay for two nights.
hotel.item.night.s1: One night in a double room is ninety dollars.
hotel.item.night.s2: We might stay an extra night if the weather is good.
hotel.item.noisy.s1: The room next to the lift is very noisy.
hotel.item.noisy.s2: It was so noisy that I couldn't sleep. Could I change rooms?
hotel.item.parking.s0: The car park is behind the hotel.
hotel.item.parking.s1: Is the car park free for guests?
hotel.item.parking.s2: The car park is full, but there's a public one across the street.
hotel.item.passport.s1: Can I see your passport, please?
hotel.item.passport.s2: We need a copy of your passport or ID card for our records.
hotel.item.phone-number.s1: My phone number is oh-nine-one, two-three-four, five-six-seven.
hotel.item.phone-number.s2: Could you leave a phone number in case we need to contact you?
hotel.item.pillow.s1: Can I have an extra pillow?
hotel.item.pillow.s2: My pillow is too hard. Do you have a softer one?
hotel.item.receptionist.s1: Ask the receptionist for the Wi-Fi password.
hotel.item.receptionist.s2: The receptionist apologised and changed our room at once.
hotel.item.reservation.note: In British English people also say "booking".
hotel.item.reservation.s1: The reservation is in the name of Brown.
hotel.item.reservation.s2: I'm afraid there's no reservation under that name.
hotel.item.river-view.s0: My room has a river view.
hotel.item.river-view.s1: A room with a river view costs a little more.
hotel.item.river-view.s2: If possible, we'd prefer a room with a river view.
hotel.item.room-service.s0: I want to call room service.
hotel.item.room-service.s1: Room service brings food to your room.
hotel.item.room-service.s2: Room service is available twenty-four hours a day.
hotel.item.second.s0: My room is on the second floor.
hotel.item.second.s1: I'm checking out on the 2nd of May.
hotel.item.second.s2: This is my second time at this hotel, and I love it.
hotel.item.shower.s1: There's no hot water in the shower.
hotel.item.shower.s2: The shower is dripping, and I can't turn it off.
hotel.item.single-room.note: A room for one person, with one bed. $60 a night.
hotel.item.single-room.s0: I'd like a single room, please.
hotel.item.single-room.s1: A single room costs sixty dollars a night.

restaurant.item.roast-chicken.s1: The roast chicken is very popular here.

school.intro: Welcome to Maple School! Learn the names of school things, subjects and days, practise classroom English and play the spelling bee.
school.item.art.s2: Our best paintings from Art are on the wall in the hall.
school.item.board.s1: The teacher writes the date on the board.
school.item.board.s2: Copy the sentences from the board into your notebook.
school.item.book.s1: Turn to page ten in your English book.
school.item.book.s2: I've forgotten my book, so I'll share with Minh.
school.item.calculator.s1: You can use a calculator in this Maths test.
school.item.calculator.s2: Try to do the sum in your head before you check it on the calculator.
school.item.classroom.s1: There are twenty desks in our classroom.
school.item.classroom.s2: We decorated the classroom with our paintings for parents' day.
school.item.count.s1: Count the books on the shelf.
school.item.count.s2: Can you count to a hundred in English without stopping?
school.item.crayon.s1: Colour the sun with a yellow crayon.
school.item.crayon.s2: The little ones love drawing with crayons on big sheets of paper.
school.item.desk.s1: Put your books on your desk.
school.item.desk.s2: I sit at the desk next to the window, so I can see the playground.
school.item.dictionary.s1: Look up the new word in your dictionary.
school.item.dictionary.s2: A good dictionary shows you how to pronounce each word.

school.item.english.s2: English is my favourite subject because I love songs and stories.

school.item.eraser.s2: If you write in pen, you can't rub it out with an eraser.

school.item.friday.s2: Everyone is happy on Friday afternoon because the weekend is coming.

school.item.history.s2: In History we're learning how people lived a thousand years ago.

school.item.maths.s2: In Maths today we learned how to add and take away big numbers.
school.item.monday.note: The first day of the school week. Days always start with a capital letter.

school.item.music.s1: I learn to play the guitar in Music.
school.item.music.s2: In Music we're practising a song for the end-of-year show.
school.item.notebook.s1: Write the new words in your notebook.
school.item.notebook.s2: I keep a notebook for new English words and read it before tests.
school.item.pe.note: PE = physical education: sport at school.

school.item.pen.s2: Please write your answers in pen, not in pencil.

school.item.timetable.s2: Our new timetable starts next week, so check which day you have PE.

sports.intro: Run, jump and play! Learn the names of sports, action words and how to talk about what you can do and what you like. Follow the coach's commands in the mini games.

sports.item.badminton.s1: In badminton, you hit a shuttlecock over a high net.
sports.item.badminton.s2: Badminton is one of the fastest racket sports in the world.

sports.item.ball.s2: The ball rolled under the bench, so we had to stop the game.
sports.item.basketball.s1: Basketball players are usually very tall.
sports.item.basketball.s2: If you want to score in basketball, you have to throw the ball through the hoop.

sports.item.catch.s2: Keep your eyes on the ball, or you won't be able to catch it.

sports.item.court.s2: We booked the indoor court because it was going to rain.

sports.item.high.s1: Can you jump higher than the bar?
sports.item.high.s2: The high jump record is higher than most doors.

sports.item.jump.s1: Can you jump higher than me?
sports.item.jump.s2: In the long jump, you run fast and then jump as far as you can.
sports.item.kick.s1: He kicked the ball into the goal.
sports.item.kick.s2: Don't kick the ball too hard, or it will go over the fence.
sports.item.martial-arts.note: do karate · do judo · do taekwondo

sports.item.match.s1: Did you watch the football match last night?

sports.item.practise.s2: If you practise more, you'll get better quickly.
sports.item.racket.s1: You need a racket for tennis and badminton.

station.item.catch.s0: I want to catch the train.
station.item.catch.s1: Hurry up! We need to catch the 8:15.
station.item.change-trains.s0: Do I need to change trains?
station.item.change-trains.s2: You have ten minutes to change trains
station.item.child-ticket.s0: One adult and one child ticket
station.item.child-ticket.s1: A child ticket is half price.
station.item.clock.s1: The clock says it's half past three.
station.item.clock.s2: The big station clock is always right
station.item.conductor.s1: Ask the conductor if this train stops at Sunny Bay.
station.item.conductor.s2: If you didn't have time to buy a ticket
station.item.delay.s1: We are sorry for the delay.
station.item.delay.s2: The delay was caused by a tree on the line after the storm.
station.item.delayed.s1: The 3:15 to Riverside is delayed by five minutes.
station.item.delayed.s2: If your train is delayed for more than an hour
station.item.departure.s1: Check the departure time on the board.
station.item.departure.s2: Please arrive at least ten minutes before departure.
station.item.departures-board.s1: The departures board shows the time and the platform.
station.item.departures-board.s2: The platform number appears on the departures board about ten minutes before the train leaves.
station.item.entrance.s1: The main entrance is on the south bank road.
station.item.entrance.s2: The side entrance is closed in the evening
station.item.exit.s1: Follow the green signs to the exit.
station.item.exit.s2: Take the exit near the bus stop if you want to catch the bus into town.
station.item.fare.s1: The fare to Sunny Bay is eight dollars.
station.item.fare.s2: Fares are higher at rush hour
station.item.footbridge.s1: Use the footbridge to get to platform 2.
station.item.footbridge.s2: Never walk across the tracks; always use the footbridge or the underpass.
station.item.get-off.s1: Get off at the third stop
station.item.get-off.s2: The doors only open for a short time
station.item.get-on.s1: Let people get off before you get on.
station.item.get-on.s2: Mind the gap between the train and the platform when you get on.
station.item.half-past.note: 2:30 = half past two. On a timetable you may see 14:30 (the 24-hour clock).
station.item.half-past.s1: The train arrives at half past six in the evening.
station.item.half-past.s2: On the timetable, half past two in the afternoon is written 14:30.
station.item.information-desk.s1: The information desk can tell you about delays.
station.item.information-desk.s2: If you need help with a wheelchair
station.item.journey.s1: The journey to Sunny Bay takes two hours.
station.item.journey.s2: The journey along the coast is beautiful
station.item.lost-property.note: In the US people say "lost and found".
station.item.lost-property.s0: Where is the lost property office?
station.item.lost-property.s1: I left my bag on the train. Can I ask at the lost property office?
station.item.lost-property.s2: Things left on trains are kept at the lost property office for three months.
station.item.luggage-trolley.s1: The luggage trolleys are next to the entrance.
station.item.luggage-trolley.s2: Please return the luggage trolley when you have finished with it.
station.item.luggage.note: Uncountable – say "a lot of luggage" or "two pieces of luggage", not "luggages".
station.item.luggage.s0: I have a lot of luggage.
station.item.luggage.s1: Please put your luggage on the rack above your seat.
station.item.luggage.s2: Don't leave your luggage alone; it may be taken away for safety reasons.
station.item.miss.s1: Don't be late or you'll miss the train.
station.item.miss.s2: I missed my train because the bus was stuck in traffic.
station.item.on-time.s2: Most trains here are on time
station.item.platform.s1: Which platform does the train to Old Town leave from?
station.item.platform.s2: Please stand behind the yellow line when a train comes into the platform.
station.item.quarter-past.note: 3:15 = quarter past three. 3:45 = quarter to four.
station.item.quarter-past.s1: The train leaves at quarter past four.
station.item.quarter-past.s2: If we miss the quarter past train
station.item.return-ticket.note: There and back again. In the US people say "round-trip ticket".
station.item.return-ticket.s2: A return ticket is usually cheaper than two single tickets.
station.item.seat-reservation.s1: Can I make a seat reservation for the 9:40 train?
station.item.seat-reservation.s2: Without a seat reservation you might have to stand on a busy train.
station.item.seat.s2: Please give your seat to someone who needs it more than you.
station.item.single-ticket.note: Only one way. In the US people say "one-way ticket".
station.item.suitcase.s0: My suitcase is big and heavy.
station.item.suitcase.s1: Can you help me carry my suitcase onto the train?
station.item.suitcase.s2: A suitcase with wheels is much easier to pull through a busy station.
station.item.ticket-machine.s1: The ticket machine takes cards and coins.
station.item.ticket-machine.s2: If the ticket machine is out of order
station.item.ticket-office.s1: You can buy tickets at the ticket office or at the machine.
station.item.ticket-office.s2: The ticket office closes at ten
station.item.ticket.s1: You need a ticket before you get on the train.
station.item.ticket.s2: Keep your ticket until the end of your journey because the conductor may check it.
station.item.timetable.note: In the US people often say "schedule".
station.item.timetable.s1: The timetable says the next train is at 3:15.
station.item.toilets.s1: The toilets are next to the waiting room.
station.item.toilets.s2: There are toilets on most trains
station.item.track.s1: The train runs on the track along the river.
station.item.train.s1: The train to Maple Hill leaves at ten past two.
station.item.train.s2: Travelling by train is relaxing because you can read or look out of the window.
station.item.underpass.s1: The underpass goes under the tracks to the other platforms.
station.item.underpass.s2: There is a lift next to the underpass for people with heavy luggage.
station.item.waiting-room.s1: You can sit in the waiting room until your train comes.
station.item.waiting-room.s2: The waiting room gets crowded when trains are delayed.
station.phrase.0: A single ticket to Riverside, please.
station.phrase.1: Can I have a return ticket to Sunny Bay?
station.phrase.10: Which platform does it leave from?
station.phrase.11: Excuse me, where are the toilets?
station.phrase.12: Go over the footbridge to platform 2.
station.phrase.13: The lost property office is next to the ticket office.
station.phrase.15: My train is delayed. When is the next one?
station.phrase.16: I've missed my train. Can I use this ticket on the next one?
station.phrase.17: I left my bag on the train.
station.phrase.19: Can I get my money back?
station.phrase.2: How much is a return ticket?
station.phrase.20: The train now arriving at platform 1 is the 2:15 to Riverside.
station.phrase.21: Please stand behind the yellow line.
station.phrase.22: We are sorry to announce that the 5:40 to Old Town is delayed.
station.phrase.23: Please mind the gap between the train and the platform.
station.phrase.24: Please do not leave your luggage unattended.
station.phrase.3: Is there a discount for children?
station.phrase.5: What time is the next train to Old Town?
station.phrase.7: How long does the journey take?
station.phrase.8: Do I need to change trains?
station.phrase.9: Is this the train to Maple Hill?
station.title: Central Station
supermarket.intro: Take a shopping list, find the products on the shelves and pay at the checkout. Learn food words, how to count them and how to talk about prices.
supermarket.item.apples.s1: I need a bag of apples.
supermarket.item.apples.s2: These apples are on sale this week.
supermarket.item.bananas.s2: Bananas are cheaper when you buy them loose.
supermarket.item.beef.note: Uncountable: some beef. Meat from a cow.
supermarket.item.beef.s2: Minced beef is good for burgers and spaghetti sauce.
supermarket.item.bread.note: Uncountable: a loaf of bread, some bread.
supermarket.item.bread.s2: The bread is baked here every morning.
supermarket.item.butter.s2: Butter gets soft quickly if you leave it out of the fridge.
supermarket.item.cake.s0: The cake is for my sister.
supermarket.item.cake.s1: Do you have chocolate birthday cakes?
supermarket.item.cake.s2: You can order a cake with a name on it.
supermarket.item.carrots.s1: Can you get a bag of carrots?
supermarket.item.carrots.s2: Carrots stay fresh for weeks if you keep them in the fridge.
supermarket.item.cereal.s2: Some cereals for children contain a lot of sugar.
supermarket.item.cheese.s1: How much is this piece of cheese?
supermarket.item.cheese.s2: The cheese counter is at the back of the shop.
supermarket.item.chicken.s2: The chicken should be kept in the fridge.
supermarket.item.chips.note: a bag of chips (British English: crisps)
supermarket.item.chips.s2: In British English, chips are called crisps.
supermarket.item.chocolate.s2: Dark chocolate has less sugar than milk chocolate.
supermarket.item.coffee.s2: Do you want ground coffee or coffee beans?
supermarket.item.cookies.note: a pack of cookies (British English: biscuits)
supermarket.item.cookies.s1: Can we buy a pack of cookies?
supermarket.item.cookies.s2: These cookies are on offer: buy one pack and get one free.
supermarket.item.croissant.s2: Croissants are cheaper after six in the evening.
supermarket.item.eggs.s2: Check that none of the eggs are broken before you buy them.
supermarket.item.fish-fingers.note: a box of fish fingers (American English: fish sticks)
supermarket.item.fish-fingers.s1: A box of fish fingers, please.
supermarket.item.fish-fingers.s2: Fish fingers are called fish sticks in American English.
supermarket.item.fish.s1: Is this fish fresh or frozen?
supermarket.item.fish.s2: Ask at the fish counter if you want it cleaned.
supermarket.item.flour.s1: We need a bag of flour for the cake.
supermarket.item.flour.s2: You can't make bread without flour.
supermarket.item.frozen-peas.s1: I need a bag of frozen peas.
supermarket.item.frozen-peas.s2: Frozen vegetables are as healthy as fresh ones.
supermarket.item.frozen-pizza.s1: Let's buy two frozen pizzas for dinner.
supermarket.item.frozen-pizza.s2: Frozen pizza is quick to cook when you don't have much time.
supermarket.item.grapes.s2: Seedless grapes are a little more expensive.
supermarket.item.ham.note: Uncountable: a pack of ham, a slice of ham.
supermarket.item.ham.s1: Can I have a pack of ham for sandwiches?
supermarket.item.ham.s2: Sliced ham must be eaten within three days of opening.
supermarket.item.honey.note: a bottle of honey (or a jar of honey)
supermarket.item.honey.s1: I'd like a bottle of honey, please.
supermarket.item.honey.s2: Local honey is more expensive, but many people say it tastes better.
supermarket.item.ice-cream.s2: Put the ice cream in the freezer as soon as you get home.
supermarket.item.juice.s1: A bottle of orange juice, please.
supermarket.item.juice.s2: Buy two bottles of juice and get one free.
supermarket.item.lettuce.s1: I need one lettuce for the salad.
supermarket.item.lettuce.s2: Lettuce stays fresh longer in the fridge.
supermarket.item.milk.s2: Is this milk full-fat or skimmed?
supermarket.item.muffins.s1: Can I have two chocolate muffins?
supermarket.item.muffins.s2: The muffins are half price at the end of the day.
supermarket.item.onions.s2: Onions are sold by weight, so put them on the scale.
supermarket.item.oranges.s1: I need a bag of oranges.
supermarket.item.oranges.s2: Oranges are full of vitamin C, so they're good for you in winter.
supermarket.item.pasta.s1: Where can I find the pasta?
supermarket.item.pasta.s2: Dried pasta lasts much longer than fresh pasta.
supermarket.item.potatoes.s2: Big potatoes are best for baking, and small ones are best for boiling.
supermarket.item.rice.s2: Brown rice takes longer to cook than white rice.
supermarket.item.sausages.s2: These sausages are made without pork.
supermarket.item.shampoo.s2: This shampoo is for dry hair.
supermarket.item.soap.s2: This soap is good for sensitive skin.
supermarket.item.soda.s1: Can I have two cans of soda?
supermarket.item.sugar.s1: Could you get a bag of sugar?
supermarket.item.sugar.s2: Brown sugar is a little more expensive than white sugar.
supermarket.item.tea.s1: We need a box of tea.
supermarket.item.tea.s2: There are a hundred tea bags in this box.
supermarket.item.tissues.s1: Can you get a box of tissues?
supermarket.item.tissues.s2: Always keep a box of tissues at home when you have a cold.
supermarket.item.toilet-paper.s1: A pack of toilet paper, please.
supermarket.item.toilet-paper.s2: The big pack is better value for money.
supermarket.item.tomatoes.s2: Keep tomatoes out of the fridge if you want them to taste better.
supermarket.item.toothpaste.s2: This toothpaste is good for sensitive teeth.
supermarket.item.water.s1: Where can I find bottled water?
supermarket.item.water.s2: A pack of six bottles is cheaper than six single ones.
supermarket.item.yogurt.s2: Plain yogurt has less sugar than fruit yogurt.
supermarket.phrase.0: Excuse me, where can I find the milk?
supermarket.phrase.1: It's in aisle three, next to the eggs.
supermarket.phrase.11: Here's your change and your receipt.
supermarket.phrase.13: It's on sale: buy one, get one free.
supermarket.phrase.14: This one is cheaper than that one.
supermarket.phrase.15: Is this the cheapest one you have?
supermarket.phrase.16: The pasta is next to the rice.
supermarket.phrase.17: We need two bags of potatoes.
supermarket.phrase.18: Buy two, get the third one half price.
supermarket.phrase.2: Do you have any fresh bread?
supermarket.phrase.3: Sorry, we've run out of bananas.
supermarket.phrase.4: How many eggs do we need?
supermarket.phrase.5: How much rice do we need?
supermarket.phrase.6: We need a carton of milk and a loaf of bread.
supermarket.title: FreshWay Supermarket
zoo.intro: Walk around the zoo, meet the animals and learn their names. Tap an animal to hear it, read about it and practise sentences.
zoo.item.beak.s0: The parrot has a strong beak.
zoo.item.beak.s1: Birds use their beaks to eat and build nests.
zoo.item.beak.s2: You can often guess what a bird eats from the shape of its beak.
zoo.item.bear.fact: Polar bears have black skin under their white fur.
zoo.item.bear.s0: The bear is brown and big.
zoo.item.bear.s2: Many bears sleep through the winter.
zoo.item.bunny.note: a child's word for a rabbit
zoo.item.bunny.s1: The bunny is eating a carrot.
zoo.item.bunny.s2: If you hold a bunny gently, it will feel safe and stay calm.
zoo.item.claw.s0: The crab has two big claws.
zoo.item.claw.s1: The bear uses its claws to climb trees.
zoo.item.claw.s2: Cats can pull their claws in when they don't need them.
zoo.item.crocodile.fact: A crocodile can't stick its tongue out.
zoo.item.crocodile.s1: The crocodile is lying in the water.
zoo.item.crocodile.s2: Crocodiles have lived on Earth since the time of the dinosaurs.
zoo.item.elephant.s1: The elephant is drinking water with its trunk.
zoo.item.elephant.s2: Elephants are known for their excellent memory.
zoo.item.enclosure.note: the area where zoo animals live (old word: cage)
zoo.item.enclosure.s1: The zebras have a big enclosure with grass.
zoo.item.enclosure.s2: Modern zoos build large enclosures that look like the animals' natural homes.
zoo.item.feather.s1: Peacocks have beautiful blue and green feathers.
zoo.item.feather.s2: Birds lose their old feathers and grow new ones every year.
zoo.item.flamingo.fact: Baby flamingos are grey, not pink.
zoo.item.flamingo.s1: The flamingo is standing on one leg.
zoo.item.flamingo.s2: Flamingos get their pink colour from the food they eat.
zoo.item.fur.s1: Its fur keeps it warm in winter.
zoo.item.fur.s2: Polar bears' fur looks white, but each hair is actually clear.
zoo.item.gift-shop.s0: Let's go to the gift shop.
zoo.item.gift-shop.s1: I bought a toy panda in the gift shop.
zoo.item.gift-shop.s2: The money from the gift shop helps to protect wild animals.
zoo.item.giraffe.fact: A giraffe's tongue is about 50 centimetres long.
zoo.item.giraffe.s0: The giraffe has a long neck.
zoo.item.giraffe.s1: Giraffes eat leaves from tall trees.
zoo.item.giraffe.s2: A giraffe only needs about two hours of sleep a day.
zoo.item.guinea-pig.fact: Guinea pigs are not pigs and they don't come from Guinea.
zoo.item.guinea-pig.s0: The guinea pig is small and brown.
zoo.item.guinea-pig.s1: Guinea pigs make funny squeaking sounds.
zoo.item.guinea-pig.s2: Guinea pigs are friendly, but they need to be handled carefully.
zoo.item.horn.s0: The rhino has a horn on its nose.
zoo.item.horn.s1: Goats have two horns on their heads.
zoo.item.horn.s2: A rhino's horn is made of the same material as our hair and nails.
zoo.item.kangaroo.note: A baby kangaroo is called a joey.
zoo.item.kangaroo.s0: The kangaroo can jump very far.
zoo.item.kangaroo.s1: The baby kangaroo lives in its mother's pouch.
zoo.item.kid.fact: Baby goats love to climb on everything.
zoo.item.kid.note: A baby goat is called a kid.
zoo.item.kid.s0: The baby goat is small and cute.
zoo.item.kid.s1: The baby goats are jumping and playing.
zoo.item.kid.s2: A baby goat can stand up just a few minutes after it is born.
zoo.item.lamb.fact: A lamb can recognise its mother's voice.
zoo.item.lamb.s0: The lamb is soft and white.
zoo.item.lamb.s1: Can I give the lamb a hug?
zoo.item.lamb.s2: Lambs stay close to their mothers for the first few months.
zoo.item.lion.fact: A lion's roar can be heard from 8 kilometres away.
zoo.item.lion.note: A male lion has a mane.
zoo.item.lion.s0: The lion is sleeping in the sun.
zoo.item.lion.s1: Lions live in groups called prides.
zoo.item.lion.s2: If you listen carefully, you can hear the lion roar.
zoo.item.mane.note: the long hair on a lion's or a horse's neck
zoo.item.mane.s0: The lion has a big mane.
zoo.item.mane.s1: The horse's mane is long and brown.
zoo.item.mane.s2: A darker mane often shows that a male lion is strong and healthy.
zoo.item.monkey.fact: Some monkeys wash their food before they eat it.
zoo.item.monkey.s0: The monkey is eating a banana.
zoo.item.monkey.s2: Some monkeys use their tails to hold on to branches.
zoo.item.panda.fact: A newborn panda is about the size of a stick of butter.
zoo.item.panda.s0: The panda is black and white.
zoo.item.panda.s1: Pandas eat bamboo almost all day.
zoo.item.panda.s2: Giant pandas spend up to 14 hours a day eating.
zoo.item.paw.note: A dog's or cat's foot is a paw.
zoo.item.paw.s1: The bear is washing its face with its paw.
zoo.item.paw.s2: A lion's paws are so big that it can knock down an animal with one hit.
zoo.item.penguin.fact: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly.
zoo.item.penguin.s2: Penguins slide on their bellies to move faster on ice.
zoo.item.tail.fact: Kangaroos use their strong tail like a fifth leg.
zoo.item.tail.s0: The monkey has a long tail.
zoo.item.tail.s1: The dog is wagging its tail.
zoo.item.tail.s2: Some lizards can grow a new tail if they lose one.
zoo.item.ticket.s1: How much is a ticket for children?
zoo.item.ticket.s2: You can save money if you buy your tickets online.
zoo.item.tiger.fact: Tigers are the biggest cats in the world.
zoo.item.tiger.s0: The tiger has orange fur and black stripes.
zoo.item.tiger.s2: No two tigers have the same stripes.
zoo.item.trunk.note: An elephant's nose is called a trunk.
zoo.item.trunk.s0: The elephant has a long trunk.
zoo.item.trunk.s1: Elephants use their trunks to drink and to say hello.
zoo.item.trunk.s2: An elephant's trunk has thousands of muscles, but no bones.
zoo.item.wing.s1: The eagle opens its wings and flies away.
zoo.item.wing.s2: Although penguins have wings, they use them to swim, not to fly.
zoo.item.zebra.fact: Every zebra has its own pattern of stripes.
zoo.item.zebra.s0: The zebra is black and white.
zoo.item.zebra.s1: Zebras live in big groups called herds.
zoo.item.zebra.s2: Scientists think the stripes help to keep flies away.
zoo.item.zoo-map.s1: Let's look at the map to find the pandas.
zoo.item.zoo-map.s2: According to the map, the gift shop is next to the exit.
zoo.item.zookeeper.s1: The zookeeper is cleaning the penguin pool.
zoo.item.zookeeper.s2: Zookeepers know every animal by name and notice when one is sick.
zoo.phrase.10: Tigers are more dangerous than pandas.
zoo.phrase.13: Are we allowed to feed the animals?
zoo.phrase.14: Please don't tap on the glass.
zoo.phrase.18: It has a long tail and soft fur.
zoo.phrase.19: The penguin's wings are shorter than the eagle's.
zoo.phrase.3: It's sleeping. Let's come back later.
zoo.phrase.6: It can swim, but it can't fly.
zoo.phrase.8: The giraffe is taller than the zebra.
zoo.phrase.9: The elephant is the biggest animal here.
zoo.title: Sunny Hills Zoo
